name: Modal

modes.label: Sandbox (gVisor), request = size, any region
modes.note: Card vCPU = Modal's own unit: Modal lists CPU per 'Physical core (2 vCPU equivalent)' at $0.00003942/s ($0.141912/h), so 1 vCPU = half a core = $0.070956/h; memory $0.00000667/GiB-s ($0.024012/GiB-h). A '4 vCPU / 8 GiB' sandbox = cpu=2, memory 8192 = $0.47592/h. Caveat: in tests cpu=N gave nproc N (hpc-sandbox-benchmarks PR #121), so cpu=2 shows 2 CPUs in the guest; the published speeds were measured at cpu=4 ($0.759744/h at 8 GiB). Rates already include the 3x non-preemptible multiplier ('Sandboxes are billed at non-preemptible rates of 3x list price', modal.com/pricing, checked 2026-11-08). Billed per second on max(request, actual): at request = W.vcpu, low utilisation saves nothing. Set cpuLimit = request: without it the soft limit is request + 16 cores and bursting is billed. GPU sandboxes are preemptible. Basis: 'You pay for `max(request, actual)`' (modal.com/docs/guide/sandbox-resources).
modes.perf_source: gVisor runtime (Modal default). StarSling requested cpu=4 and the sandbox saw 4 CPUs (https://github.com/starslingdev/hpc-sandbox-benchmarks/pull/121); Modal prices 1 physical core = 2 vCPU, so match price and speed with care. CPU 12.6 runs/s: V8 Web Tooling Benchmark (Phoronix node-web-tooling), StarSling hpc-sandbox-benchmarks run 37073680030 (2026-10-03), row "Modal (gVisor)", median of 5 sandboxes at a 4 vCPU / 8 GB target, rank 7 of 15 (shared: the run cannot separate it from the providers at the same rank). https://github.com/starslingdev/hpc-sandbox-benchmarks/blob/297198a96ee827df5edcd918bd37b949526cfe20/LEADERBOARD.md ComputeSDK (each provider at its SDK default size and runtime): burst 796 ms median at 100 at once, 100% succeeded (2026-11-06); DAX clone + install + typecheck 96.33 s (2026-11-06, one run; sandbox saw 4 CPUs / 329 GiB x86); one-at-a-time start 549 ms (sequential TTI, latest published run 2026-08-07 or older). https://github.com/computesdk/benchmarks/tree/main/results

modes.label: Sandbox, minimal request + burst (billed ~ on usage; burst capacity not guaranteed)
modes.note: The request is set to the minimum (cpu 0.125 core = 0.25 card-vCPU at Modal's 1 core = 2 vCPU; 128 MiB) and cpu/memory limits are set to the workload size, so the guest sees W.vcpu CPUs (nproc = ceil(limit)). Billing is max(request, actual) per second, so it tracks usage. active_floor 0.0625 = 0.25 vCPU / 4 vCPU (the exact floor is 0.25/W.vcpu). Burst capacity is NOT guaranteed (it needs spare host capacity), so the workload may be throttled. The memory limit is a hard OOM. Optimistic regime. Floor verified 2026-09-28: 'minimum of 0.125 cores per container' (modal.com/pricing); 'a default request of 0.125 CPU cores and 128 MiB of memory' (modal.com/docs/guide/resources). Docs do not say whether page cache counts toward memory usage. ASSUMES a small CPU/memory request (0.125 core / 128 MiB): guaranteed capacity is only that request; anything above it is best-effort burst. Memory above the request is not guaranteed either: Modal can EVICT a sandbox that exceeds its memory request (docs recommend requesting p90-95 of memory), so the RAM half of this regime is optimistic and can kill the session; only CPU is safe to under-request.

plans.name: Starter
plans.note: $30/mo included compute; max 3 seats (no paid extra seats listed); 100 containers, 10 GPU concurrency; egress 1 TiB/mo free; payment method required; overage auto-charged (spend limit optional, hard stop). GPU concurrency 10 (modal.com/pricing, 2026-09-28); non-spec key gpu_concurrency (engine plan.concurrency holds the 100-container cap).

plans.name: Team
plans.note: $250 fee of which only $100 returns as compute credit; unlimited seats; 5,000 containers, 50 GPU concurrency; egress 10 TiB/mo free (engine network block uses Starter's 1 TiB); static IP proxy; custom domains; environment budgets.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Custom pricing: volume discounts, compute reservations, AWS/GCP marketplace committed spend; egress 100 TiB/mo free; HIPAA compatibility (Enterprise only; no BAA named on the pricing page), SSO, audit logs; 100k+ concurrent sandboxes cited in Modal blog.

perf_source: Two runtimes (gVisor here, VM on the separate GA card "Modal (VM Sandboxes)"): perf is per mode.

knobs.label: Region pin

options.label: Broad region pin: us / eu / ap (×1.15)
Narrow region pin: us-east, uk, jp ... (×1.75)

knobs.why: Modal multiplies all sandbox resource charges (incl. GPU) by 1.15x for a broad-region pin and 1.75x for a narrow-region pin; data residency (e.g. EU) requires a pin. Applied only to modes without a baked multiplier (region-broad / region-narrow already carry 1.15 / 1.75). VM Sandbox excluded: whether the multiplier applies there is not stated.

knobs.label: Idle time billed before idle_timeout / timeout ends the sandbox (× session hours)
knobs.why: Modal has no paused state: an idle sandbox pays its full request (max(request, actual)) until idle_timeout or timeout (default 5 min, max 24 h) terminates it, or you call terminate(). Default 1 = you terminate as soon as work ends; the 2x ceiling is a judgment call.

caveats: How we count Modal's CPU: we use Modal's own published unit, 1 physical core = 2 vCPU ('Physical core (2 vCPU equivalent)', modal.com/pricing; 'The cpu parameter specifies physical CPU cores (1 core = 2 vCPUs)', modal.com/docs/guide/sandbox-resources). This is the lowest Modal price Modal's own pages support: 1 vCPU = $0.070956/h, and 4 vCPU / 8 GiB = cpu=2 = $0.47592/h. Know this before you size: cpu=N gives the sandbox N CPUs (hpc-sandbox-benchmarks PR #121, ComputeSDK), so cpu=2 shows 2 CPUs. If your code needs 4 CPUs, request cpu=4: $0.759744/h at 8 GiB. The published perf numbers were measured at cpu=4. Rule: FAIRNESS.md, 'CPU units'. Evidence: research/verify/modal-cpu.md.
free.monthly_credit ($30) IS the Starter plan's included_usd, so don't subtract both. Team replaces it with $100 included.

Billing is max(request, actual). The on-demand mode assumes request = workload size, so cpu_util gives no saving. Low-request-burst is optimistic: burst depends on spare host capacity, and its active_floor (0.0625) is exact only for 4 vCPU (0.25 vCPU = 0.125 core, / W.vcpu).

Uncapped burst can bill MORE than the requested size (default soft limit is request + 16 cores) and the gVisor guest then reports ceil(limit) CPUs (ComputeSDK DAX 2026-07-17 at SDK defaults: nproc 17). The engine can't model this; set cpu=(req, limit).

Egress at $0.04/GiB is charged only from 2026-10-01 (tracked, not billed, in Sep 2026). The allowance is plan-dependent (Starter 1 TiB, Team 10 TiB, Enterprise 100 TiB) and counts private container-to-container traffic and Cloud Bucket Mount uploads.

Snapshot storage (filesystem/directory/memory) price is not published, so snapshot_gib_month is null. Filesystem snapshots default to a 30-day TTL (configurable/indefinite). Memory snapshots (alpha) expire after 7 days and terminate the source sandbox.

Ephemeral disk: 512 GiB default quota, max 3 TiB. An explicit disk request is billed by raising the memory request to disk/20 GiB, so it costs extra only when disk/20 > the memory request. disk_gib_month is null because it is not a flat rate.

No pause/stopped state. Default timeout is 5 min, max 24 h. Idle sandboxes pay the full request until idle_timeout terminates them. To keep work, your code calls snapshot_filesystem() (whole root disk; 30-day default TTL, configurable or indefinite) or writes to a Volume, then starts a new sandbox from it.
GPU sandboxes are preemptible. GPU concurrency is 10 (Starter) and 50 (Team). H100->H200 and A100-40->80 auto-upgrades are billed at the requested type's price.
Volumes cost $0.09/GiB-month beyond 1 TiB free (not modelled in the storage block).
Enterprise discounts and reservations are unpublished. Startup credits are unpublished. Academic grants are up to $10k one-time (not in free.one_time_credit).
Max vCPU/RAM per sandbox is not published (the docs say a max is enforced). A third-party snippet cites 64 cores / 336 GB per container.
Adjacent option not in modes: running the same code as a preemptible Modal Function costs 1/3 of the sandbox rate ($0.04716/vCPU-h per cpu unit, $0.007992/GiB-h), but it isn't a sandbox.

perf is mode-level (card-level nulled): gVisor modes from HPC and ComputeSDK runs; VM runtime on the card "Modal (VM Sandboxes)". The HPC runs and ComputeSDK DAX passed cpu=4/cpuLimit=4 and observed nproc=4. The card prices '4 vCPU' as cpu=2 (Modal's 1 core = 2 vCPU), so the measured shape costs $0.759744/h at 8 GiB, not the $0.47592/h priced. See research/perf-costs.md.

GPU counts (https://modal.com/docs/guide/gpu): A10 max 4 per container; T4/L4/L40S/A100/H100/H200/B200/B300 max 8; RTX PRO 6000 count unverified. H100 requests may be upgraded to H200 (billed as H100), B200 to B300 (billed as B200). GPU charge is not reduced by CPU utilisation in the low-request-burst mode.

Egress: not charged in September 2026 (usage shown only). From 2026-10-01 egress is $0.04/GiB beyond 1 TiB (Starter) / 10 TiB (Team) / 100 TiB (Enterprise) per workspace per billing cycle; first invoice 2026-11-01. Card uses the current (free) rate; switch egress_gib to 0.04 on 2026-10-01 and add plan egress_free_gib 10240 on Team. https://modal.com/docs/guide/network-egress-billing

GPU concurrency caps: Starter 10, Team 50, Enterprise custom (modal.com/pricing, 2026-09-28). The engine plan concurrency is the container cap (100 / 5,000); a workload with >10 concurrent GPU sandboxes needs Team.

Snapshot storage re-checked 2026-09-28 (modal.com/docs/guide/sandbox-snapshots): retention is documented (filesystem/directory 30 days default, memory 7 days) but no price; snapshot_gib_month stays null.

Features check 2026-09-28: card.features.docker_inside true -> null for the default gVisor runtime. Current docs only document Docker via VM Sandboxes ("VM Sandboxes are also the recommended method to run Docker in Sandboxes", modal.com/docs/guide/vm-sandboxes); no current doc statement that Docker runs under gVisor. vm-sandbox mode keeps docker_inside true. nested_virt stays false in all modes: VM Sandboxes "Nested KVM virtualization is disabled by default. Please reach out to us if you'd like access."

Included compute ($30 Starter / $100 Team) applies to Functions, Sandboxes and Notebooks CPU/memory/GPU; Volumes have their own 1 TiB; Shared Endpoint tokens are billed from the first request (since 2026-09-01). Whether egress overage is covered by included compute is not stated.
Volumes: storage is sampled once a day and deleted data may still be billed for up to 4 days.
Sidecars (public alpha, Sep 2026) share the Sandbox's CPU/memory request; there is no separate sidecar charge but the request must cover all containers.
VM Sandboxes (real kernel: Docker, FUSE, eBPF; GA 2026-10-01, same prices, no GPU) are the separate card "Modal (VM Sandboxes)".

Desktop, browser and computer use: no built-in product. Modal's official example installs Xvfb, Chromium, x11vnc and noVNC and drives Browser Use (https://modal.com/docs/examples/computer_use_vnc, checked 2026-11-08). The example runs on the VM runtime.
Nested virtualization: VM runtime only, Enterprise plan, experimental option (https://modal.com/docs/guide/vm-sandboxes, checked 2026-11-08).

fleet.tiers: Starter 100 concurrent containers / 10 GPUs; Team ($250/month) 5,000 containers / 50 GPUs; Enterprise custom.
fleet.notes: Pricing checked against current official page; old 1,000 Team-container claims are stale. 10/50 CPU fleet fits Starter, 300/1,000 Team within quota, not a reservation. GPU count is total GPUs concurrently used, confirmed by scale guide, not GPU-container count. Per-Function hard cap 4,000 distinct from workspace total. No approval SLA. New-account spend ceiling: the Workspace budget maximum grows only after successful incremental charges, and usage stops at the limit. SDK 1.6.0 (2026-09-28) made the v2 Sandbox backend default with 'substantially higher creation rates and concurrency limits for CPU Sandboxes'; Sandbox.create raises ResourceExhaustedError if unschedulable. No numeric creation-rate limit is published; the pricing page still lists 100 (Starter) / 5000 (Team) containers.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Snapshots are triggered from outside the Sandbox, typically just before termination.
snapshot_auto.note: Timeout (max 24 h) and idle_timeout terminate the sandbox; no pause/sleep state and no automatic checkpoint. Docs tell you to call snapshot_filesystem() yourself before terminating and restore into a new sandbox.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Sandbox memory snapshots are copies of a Sandbox’s entire state, both in memory and on the filesystem. These Snapshots can be restored later to create a new Sandbox, which is an exact clone of the original Sandbox.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Filesystem snapshots (GA, snapshot_filesystem(), disk only, become Images that boot any number of new sandboxes; 30-day default TTL, ttl=None for indefinite) and directory snapshots (mount into running sandboxes). Memory snapshots (_experimental_snapshot, alpha): RAM + FS, but snapshotting terminates the sandbox, no GPU, 7-day expiry; restore via _experimental_from_snapshot creates a clone. VM-runtime memory snapshots only for enabled customers.

harness_api.quote: Run a background coding agent with OpenCode
harness_api.note: Only examples (OpenCode server, Claude Agent SDK, Cursor Cloud Agents) built on generic exec/tunnels; no first-party API to start/stream/resume a harness. Modal is an execution backend for Anthropic's Claude Managed Agents (harness driven by Anthropic, not a Modal API). Sidecars doc mentions 'Separating an agent harness from its execution environment' as a pattern only.

egress_allowlist.quote:
| **IP-range allowlist**        | `outbound_cidr_allowlist`   | Only allows traffic to the listed CIDR ranges (any protocol).  |
| **Domain allowlist** *(Beta)* | `outbound_domain_allowlist` | Only allows TLS traffic (port 443) to the listed domain names. |
egress_allowlist.note: Also block_network=True (no internet). Domain allowlist is SNI-based (beta, wildcards), Modal resolves hostname itself; experimental runtime updates of allowlists without restart.

egress_http_rules.quote: TLS traffic is not decrypted, so the `Host` header, URL path, and body are never inspected.
egress_http_rules.note: Built-in controls are host/IP only. DIY option: experimental proxy_traffic_via_sidecar routes all port-443 traffic to a user-run Sidecar (alpha, allowlisted workspaces) where you can run e.g. mitmproxy for method/path filtering; that is user-operated, not a provider rule engine.

ingress_rules.quote:
Use `inbound_cidr_allowlist` to restrict which IP addresses can connect
**inbound** to the Sandbox through tunnels and Sandbox Connect Tokens:
ingress_rules.note: Default: no inbound. Ports exposed explicitly (encrypted_ports/h2_ports/unencrypted_ports); Sandbox Connect Tokens give authenticated HTTP/WebSocket access with an unspoofable X-Verified-User-Data header.

guest_firewall.quote: gVisor, a container runtime developed by Google, provides strong isolation and is suitable for most workloads.
guest_firewall.note: Not published for gVisor: the old evidence was the VM runtime's own kernel, which this card does not cover. No Modal page documents iptables/nftables inside a gVisor sandbox. VM runtime: card "Modal (VM Sandboxes)".

systemd.quote: They run a real Linux kernel, so they can support workloads that run Docker containers within the Sandbox, or that require Linux features like eBPF, systemd, cgroups, or custom filesystem mounts.
systemd.note: Modal names systemd as a reason to use VM Sandboxes ("They" = VM Sandboxes). Same basis as fuse and kernel_features false on this gVisor card. VM runtime: card "Modal (VM Sandboxes)".

secret_proxy.quote:
Rather than passing that key into the Sandbox,
you can keep it in a separate, trusted container and let that container add it to
outbound requests
secret_proxy.note: No managed credential-injecting proxy. modal.Secret = env vars injected into the container. A DIY pattern exists: run your own proxy (Caddy/nginx/Envoy/mitmproxy) as a Sidecar holding the Secret, optionally forced via proxy_traffic_via_sidecar; this can cover any HTTP API but you build/operate it; Sidecars are alpha and restricted to allowlisted workspaces.

volume_attach.quote: Volumes are a high-performance distributed file system for Modal applications.
volume_attach.note: modal.Volume mounted via volumes={...} on Sandbox.create; also CloudBucketMount (S3/R2/GCS, read-write or read_only) and deprecated NetworkFileSystem. Distributed FS with explicit commit/reload semantics, not a block device.

volume_shared.quote:
Concurrent modification from multiple containers is supported, but concurrent
modifications of the same files should be avoided. Last write wins
volume_shared.note: Read-write (or read_only mount option); sub_path mounts isolate sessions on one Volume; v2 volumes: concurrent writes from hundreds of containers. Changes visible to others only after commit + reload. Bucket mounts also shareable.

docker_inside.quote: Use the VM runtime to run Docker in a Sandbox. Start `dockerd` as the Sandbox entrypoint and run containers with `sb.exec`.
docker_inside.note: True only under the VM Sandbox runtime (runtime="vm", generally available since 2026-10-01: "Starting today, VM Sandboxes are generally available on Modal", https://modal.com/blog/vm-sandboxes-agent-computers); the gVisor runtime is not documented to support running Docker/dockerd inside it. This card covers gVisor; VM is the separate card "Modal (VM Sandboxes)". Pin runtime="gvisor" explicitly: the VM guide says "Switch runtimes via the `runtime` parameter, or leave unset to let Modal choose for you." (https://modal.com/docs/guide/vm-sandboxes).

anti_bot.quote: Modal is a platform for running AI workloads in the cloud with minimal configuration. Key use cases include AI model training and inference, high-performance batch jobs, and sandboxed code execution.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Modal is a general compute/sandbox platform, not a browser-automation/scraping product; no stealth or fingerprint-evasion feature is documented.

captcha_solving.quote: Modal is a platform for running AI workloads in the cloud with minimal configuration. Key use cases include AI model training and inference, high-performance batch jobs, and sandboxed code execution.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No CAPTCHA-solving feature or API is documented anywhere in Modal's docs/pricing.

egress_ip_type.quote: Proxies are a secure tunnel between Apps and exit nodes with static IPs. You can allow-list those static IPs in your network firewall...
egress_ip_type.note: Team/Enterprise-plan Proxy feature gives fixed outbound datacenter IPs (WireGuard exit nodes); default (no Proxy) egress uses Modal's shared cloud-provider datacenter IP ranges, which vary by run.

fork_running.quote: Since Filesystem Snapshots are Images, you can create multiple Sandboxes from the same snapshot.
fork_running.note: The terminate rule ('Snapshotting a Sandbox will currently cause it to terminate') is under Memory Snapshots only. The filesystem snapshot docs do not say whether the source keeps running: every example calls terminate() right after snapshot_filesystem(). Not confirmed either way.

wake_on_request.quote: Sandboxes can also be automatically terminated after a period of inactivity - you can do this by setting the `idle_timeout` parameter.
wake_on_request.note: Sandboxes have no sleep/paused state: idle_timeout or timeout fully terminates the Sandbox (Finished state); there is no mechanism for a stopped sandbox to wake automatically on an incoming request. Consistent with card caveat 'No pause/stopped state.'

live_resize.quote: Physical core (2 vCPU equivalent)... You pay for max(request, actual). ... a default request of 0.125 CPU cores and 128 MiB of memory
live_resize.note: CPU/memory are set via request/limit parameters at Sandbox.create() time (with elastic bursting up to a limit); no documented API to change a running Sandbox's resource request/limit after creation without recreating it. The Sandbox SDK reference (Sandbox.md) has no update/resize method.

own_agent_api.quote: Modal is a platform for running AI workloads in the cloud with minimal configuration. Key use cases include AI model training and inference, high-performance batch jobs, and sandboxed code execution.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Modal is an execution backend that lets customers run their own agents/harnesses (examples: OpenCode, Claude Agent SDK, Cursor Cloud Agents); it does not ship its own first-party browser/computer-use/research task agent.

mcp_server.quote: This example demonstrates how to deploy a simple MCP server on Modal with FastMCP.
mcp_server.note: Modal's MCP-related material is an example of hosting a user-built MCP server on Modal, not a first-party MCP server Modal ships to let clients control Modal Sandboxes/Apps themselves. No such control-plane MCP server is documented in the CLI or guide sections of llms.txt.

lang_node.quote: Modal offers official SDKs in Python, Go, and JavaScript/TypeScript, along with a fully-featured CLI for interacting with the platform.
lang_node.note: First-party JS/TypeScript SDK (modal.com/docs/sdk/js/latest/intro.md, beta) exposes Sandbox/Function/etc.; Node.js also runs inside sandboxes generically via custom images (e.g. 'Run Node.js, Ruby, and more in a Sandbox' example).

byoc.quote: Compute jobs at Modal are containerized and virtualized using gVisor... Sandboxes may also run on Modal's secure VM runtime.
byoc.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Modal is a fully managed multi-tenant serverless platform running on its own infrastructure/regions; no self-hosted-in-your-cloud-account (BYOC) deployment option is documented on the security, pricing, or enterprise pages.

eu_data_residency.quote: You can select the container and routing regions for most Modal services... For a full list of available regions, please visit our region selection documentation page.
eu_data_residency.note: Region selection documents an 'eu' broad region (European Economic Area) with eu-west/eu-north/eu-south narrow regions; Sandboxes support container-region pinning to 'eu' (region-selection.md), which the card's region-broad/region-narrow modes price at 1.15x/1.75x.

persistent_disk.quote: Snapshots are triggered from outside the Sandbox, typically just before termination.
persistent_disk.how: snapshot the root filesystem before the sandbox ends and boot the next one from it; Volumes keep one folder with no snapshot
persistent_disk.note: The root disk itself ends with the sandbox. Your code keeps it through a filesystem snapshot (whole disk) or a Volume (one folder, https://modal.com/docs/guide/volumes).

pause_resume.quote: 5. **Finished** — The Sandbox has stopped running. This can happen for several reasons: the entrypoint process exited on its own, the Sandbox was explicitly terminated (via the dashboard or `sandbox.terminate()`), the timeout or idle timeout was reached, or an out-of-memory condition occurred. Once finished, no further commands can be executed inside the Sandbox.
pause_resume.note: Sandbox lifecycle only has Created/Scheduled/Started/Ready/Finished; there is no Paused state and no resume of a running container. (Filesystem/memory snapshot+restore exists but that creates a brand-new Sandbox, not a resumed one — tracked separately as memory_snapshot_fork.)

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Sandbox memory snapshots are copies of a Sandbox's entire state, both in memory and on the filesystem. These Snapshots can be restored later to create a new Sandbox, which is an exact clone of the original Sandbox.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Memory Snapshots (alpha, gated: 'Access to VM Memory Snapshots is available on request') capture RAM+FS and Sandbox._experimental_from_snapshot() clones them into a new, running Sandbox with processes' memory state intact -- this is exactly the memory_snapshot_fork definition. Alpha/experimental API (_experimental_snapshot / _experimental_enable_snapshot), so confidence medium rather than high.

nested_virt.quote: Nested virtualization is available on the Enterprise plan ... by setting `experimental_options={"enable_nested_virt": True}` on a VM Sandbox.
nested_virt.note: Not on gVisor. VM runtime only (card "Modal (VM Sandboxes)"), Enterprise plan, experimental option.

ssh.quote: This assumes you have a rsa keypair in ~/.ssh/id_rsa{.pub}, this is a bare-bones example letting you SSH into a Modal container. ... subprocess.Popen(["/usr/sbin/sshd", "-D", "-e"]) with modal.forward(port=22, unencrypted=True) as tunnel: ... connection_cmd = f'ssh -p {port} root@{hostname}'
ssh.note: Documented pattern, not a managed SSH endpoint: you supply sshd and keys.
ssh.how: install openssh-server in the image, run sshd and expose port 22 with modal.forward (official example)

desktop.quote: In each Sandbox, Xvfb provides a virtual display, x11vnc serves it over VNC, and websockify bridges the stream into the noVNC page that the UI embeds.
desktop.how: install Xvfb, x11vnc and noVNC in the sandbox image (official example, runs on the VM runtime)

browser.quote: The agent drives Chromium inside a Modal Sandbox running in a VM
browser.how: install Chromium in the sandbox image (official example)

computer_use.quote: Computer-use agents are LLMs that can interact with a web browser in a loop. ... This example builds one with Browser Use.
computer_use.how: run Browser Use against Chromium on an Xvfb display in the sandbox (official example); no first-party screenshot/click API

public_ipv4.quote: Sandboxes are built to be secure-by-default, meaning that a default Sandbox has no ability to accept incoming network connections or access your Modal resources.
public_ipv4.note: Inbound access is only via TLS tunnels/hostnames (modal.forward, encrypted_ports, Connect Tokens) or workspace-private i6pn IPv6 for clusters; there is no per-sandbox public IPv4 assigned. The 'static IP' feature (Proxies, already features.static_egress_ip=true) is for outbound traffic only ('Proxies are a secure tunnel between Apps and exit nodes with static IPs'), not an inbound public IPv4 on the machine.

agent_harnesses.quote: First, we define a Modal container Image with OpenCode installed. ... .run_commands("curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash")
agent_harnesses.note: Official example 'Run OpenCode in a Modal Sandbox' installs OpenCode with one image command. Modal does not preinstall harnesses.
agent_harnesses.how: install the harness in the image, for example OpenCode with run_commands (official example)

windows.quote: By default, Modal Functions and Sandboxes run in a Debian Linux environment with a basic Python installation of the same minor version `v3.x` as your local Python interpreter.
windows.note: No Windows runtime or Windows base images are offered anywhere in the docs; Sandboxes/Functions are Linux containers/VMs (Debian-based, or custom OCI Linux images) only.

macos.quote: By default, Modal Functions and Sandboxes run in a Debian Linux environment
macos.note: Modal is a Linux-container/VM compute platform (gVisor or Linux-kernel VM runtimes); no macOS machines/images are offered. Plainly outside the product, matching the 'macOS for a GPU cloud' example in the field definitions.

arm64.quote: The image must be built for the `linux/amd64` platform.
arm64.note: Docs require linux/amd64 for custom images and never mention arm64/aarch64/Graviton/Apple-silicon guest CPUs anywhere in the docs, GPU guide, or pricing page; the only architecture named across the full llms-full.txt corpus is x86_64/amd64 (e.g. flash-attn wheels are linux_x86_64, binaries are linux-amd64). Treated as x86_64-only.

self_host.quote: Most interactions with Modal are well-described in a gRPC API, and occur through modal, our open-source command-line tool and Python client library.
self_host.note: Only the client (CLI/SDK) is open; the actual compute platform (workers, scheduler, storage) is Modal's own multi-tenant SaaS with no on-prem/self-hosted or BYOC deployment option documented anywhere (Enterprise plan mentions AWS/GCP marketplace billing, not deploying Modal's control plane into a customer's account).

open_source.quote: occur through modal, our open-source command-line tool and Python client library.
open_source.note: Only the `modal` CLI/Python client is open-source; the core product -- the compute platform itself (scheduler, workers, storage, billing) -- is closed-source and only usable as Modal's hosted service. No OSI license covers the core product.

cpu_class.quote: Sandboxes can burst beyond their CPU and memory requests when additional resources are available on the underlying host. Your request guarantees a minimum level of resources, but when spare capacity exists, your Sandbox can use more. You pay for `max(request, actual)`.
cpu_class.note: Modal guarantees the requested number of physical cores ('access to at least N cores', modal.com/docs/guide/resources) -- i.e. reserved/dedicated capacity up to the request, with additional cores above that available only opportunistically (soft limit request+16 cores, throttled beyond it) and billed via max(request,actual). For on-demand/region-*/vm-sandbox modes the request is set to the workload size, so the guaranteed (dedicated) portion covers the whole workload. For low-request-burst the request is deliberately set to the minimum (0.125 core) and the card's own note says burst capacity is NOT guaranteed ('it needs spare host capacity ... the workload may be throttled'), so most of that mode's effective vCPUs are best-effort/shared rather than reserved.

fast_boot.note: ComputeSDK burst run 2026-11-06 (gVisor runtime, SDK default): 100 at once, p95 1,648 ms, 100% started. Modal's own claim: "sub-second cold-starts" (https://modal.com/blog/vm-sandboxes-agent-computers).

usage_api.quote: The card lists billing and budgets guides as sources but does not provide specific evidence of a REST API, SDK method, or CLI command that returns per-sandbox or per-tag billable usage. Modal's pricing page and billing docs do not document a programmatic usage/metrics endpoint in the available card
usage_api.note: Modal ships a Python SDK and CLI but the card's sources do not cite a specific usage_api endpoint, method, or CLI command. Verification requires checking modal.com/docs/guide/billing and the SDK reference directly for methods like get_usage(), usage API endpoints, or billing export formats. The card's 'budgets' feature (plan-level spend limits) is documented but distinct from usage reporting.

persist_scope.quote: Filesystem Snapshots are copies of the Sandbox's root filesystem at a given point in time. ... You can configure a custom TTL when creating a snapshot, or opt out of expiry entirely to retain snapshots indefinitely.
persist_scope.how: call snapshot_filesystem() before the sandbox ends, then start the next sandbox from that image; or mount a Volume for one folder
persist_scope.note: The snapshot is the whole root filesystem, installed packages included (mounted Volumes are not in it). Default TTL 30 days, configurable or indefinite. Snapshot storage price is not published. No paused state: a new sandbox starts from the image.

fuse.quote: Reach for runtime="vm" when you butt against the walls of userspace: Docker, FUSE filesystems, or niche Linux kernel features.
fuse.note: On gVisor FUSE does not mount (Legora: "running code sandboxes as bare processes because FUSE wouldn’t mount"); use the VM card.

kernel_features.quote: Reach for runtime="vm" when you butt against the walls of userspace: Docker, FUSE filesystems, or niche Linux kernel features.

sidecar.quote: Sandbox Sidecars let you run additional containers alongside your main Sandbox container, on the same host.
sidecar.note: Beta. Each sidecar "runs in a separate, sandboxed process isolated from the main Sandbox container", reachable by name over an internal bridge network; up to 250 per sandbox, sharing the sandbox’s CPU/memory. CPU-only even when the sandbox has a GPU.

hipaa.note: Enterprise plan only: the pricing table ticks HIPAA compatibility for Enterprise, not Starter or Team. The pricing page does not mention a BAA.

burst.quote: Sandboxes can burst beyond their CPU and memory requests when additional resources are available on the underlying host. Your request guarantees a minimum level of resources, but when spare capacity exists, your Sandbox can use more. You pay for `max(request, actual)`.
burst.note: Billed per second for max(request, used): a sandbox can use more than it reserved. Bursting is best effort, not guaranteed capacity.

locations_quote: Modal offers different levels of granularity for container regions. Broad... us, eu, ap. Narrow: us-east, us-central, us-south, us-west, eu-west, eu-north, eu-south, ap-northeast, ap-southeast, ap-south, ap-melbourne, jp, au, uk, ca, sa, af, mx
